synthesis: Recent verified developments show the national laboratory competitors pushing beyond routine testing into consumer genetics, embedded oncology workflows and higher-sensitivity specialty diagnostics while maintaining strong core financial performance. Labcorp reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.731 billion, up 5.8%, adjusted EPS of $4.99, up 14.9%, and reported operating margin of 12.1% versus 11.2% a year earlier. Adjusted operating margin reached 15.8%; Diagnostics Laboratories adjusted margin was 18.0% and Biopharma Laboratory Services adjusted margin was 17.0%, showing operating leverage alongside growth. Labcorp raised enterprise revenue-growth guidance to 5.4%–6.3% and adjusted EPS guidance to $18.10–$18.55. Its Marker by Labcorp Genetic Health Panel extends the company into direct-to-consumer hereditary-risk testing: the panel analyzes 163 genes linked to more than 100 medically actionable conditions, became available through Labcorp OnDemand on August 3, and combines nationwide blood collection with genetic counseling and digital result delivery. Quest remains stronger on recent top-line momentum, with second-quarter revenue up 10.2% to $3.043 billion, 10.0% organic growth, requisition volume up 13.1% and adjusted EPS up 19.1% to $3.12, followed by higher full-year guidance. Quest is also embedding Haystack MRD and comprehensive genomic profiling into Flatiron Health’s OncoEMR MPI; the completed integration is intended to reach about 4,700 clinicians across 1,600 community oncology locations, beginning with an American Oncology Network pilot. ARUP Laboratories added a differentiated hematopathology capability with ARUP CLARISPECT Multiple Myeloma MRD by Spectral Flow Cytometry, which uses an 18-marker single-tube design and can detect as few as 14 neoplastic cells among 5 million analyzed cells with 95% confidence. The competitive direction is increasingly defined by specialized diagnostics that combine analytical sensitivity, consumer or clinician workflow access, and scalable distribution, with margin execution remaining an important differentiator alongside laboratory volume.

companies.Labcorp: Labcorp is combining margin improvement and raised 2026 guidance with expansion into consumer genetics and therapy-linked diagnostics. Second-quarter revenue rose 5.8% to $3.731 billion and adjusted EPS increased 14.9% to $4.99. Reported operating margin improved to 12.1% from 11.2%, adjusted operating margin reached 15.8%, Diagnostics Laboratories adjusted margin was 18.0% and Biopharma Laboratory Services adjusted margin was 17.0%. The company raised enterprise revenue-growth guidance to 5.4%–6.3% and adjusted EPS guidance to $18.10–$18.55. Marker by Labcorp adds direct consumer access to a 163-gene hereditary-risk panel covering more than 100 medically actionable conditions, supported by more than 2,200 patient service centers, digital result delivery and licensed genetic counseling. This broadens Labcorp’s growth platform beyond routine testing into higher-value genetics while complementing recent PTEN companion-diagnostic, DPYD, ColoSense and oncology initiatives.
companies.Quest Diagnostics: Quest continues to pair stronger organic growth with deeper integration into consumer and oncology channels. Second-quarter revenue increased 10.2% to $3.043 billion, organic revenue rose 10.0%, requisition volume increased 13.1% and adjusted EPS rose 19.1% to $3.12, prompting higher 2026 revenue and EPS guidance. Post-results analyst estimates also moved higher, reinforcing the financial momentum, although those forecasts remain external expectations rather than company guidance. The OncoEMR MPI initiative embeds Haystack MRD and comprehensive genomic profiling into existing community-oncology workflows, with an eventual addressable network of about 4,700 clinicians across 1,600 locations and an active pilot that includes nearly 200 American Oncology Network sites. The move reinforces Quest’s strategy of making advanced diagnostics easier to order and consume inside established clinical workflows while its consumer and wellness partnerships create additional access points outside traditional physician channels.
companies.ARUP Laboratories: ARUP Laboratories strengthened its specialty-testing differentiation with the launch of ARUP CLARISPECT Multiple Myeloma MRD by Spectral Flow Cytometry. ARUP says it is the first large U.S. reference laboratory to offer spectral flow technology for clinical use. The assay uses 18 markers in a single-tube design, lowers specimen-volume requirements and can detect as few as 14 neoplastic cells among 5 million analyzed cells with 95% confidence. The launch gives ARUP a distinctive position in high-sensitivity multiple-myeloma MRD assessment and establishes a platform the laboratory plans to extend to additional spectral-flow MRD assays.

categories.Financials: Labcorp and Quest both raised 2026 outlooks after strong second quarters, but Quest continues to lead on recent organic and volume momentum. Labcorp revenue grew 5.8% and adjusted EPS 14.9%, while its reported operating margin improved 90 basis points to 12.1% and adjusted operating margin reached 15.8%. Quest revenue grew 10.2%, organic revenue 10.0%, requisition volume 13.1% and adjusted EPS 19.1%. Labcorp’s segment margin expansion shows stronger operating leverage even as Quest remains ahead on recent top-line growth.
categories.Product & Services: Labcorp’s Marker genetic-health panel brings a 163-gene, 100-plus-condition hereditary-risk offering into its direct-to-consumer OnDemand channel. Quest is embedding Haystack MRD and comprehensive genomic profiling into Flatiron Health’s OncoEMR workflow. ARUP launched a spectral-flow multiple-myeloma MRD assay with an 18-marker single-tube design and very high analytical sensitivity.
categories.Clinical, R&D: Recent verified activity reinforces the shift toward higher-sensitivity and therapy-relevant diagnostics. ARUP’s spectral-flow MRD assay is designed to characterize very small residual multiple-myeloma populations, while Quest’s Haystack MRD workflow expansion increases clinician access to ctDNA-based residual-disease testing in community oncology. Labcorp continues to build therapy-linked oncology testing alongside its broader specialty portfolio.
categories.Partnerships & M&A: Quest’s OncoEMR MPI integration with Flatiron Health and pilot with American Oncology Network illustrate a partnership model focused on embedding advanced testing directly into care delivery. Labcorp invested $225.7 million in acquisitions during the second quarter, while its recent product expansion also leverages genetics capabilities acquired from Invitae.
categories.Leadership & Organization: Quest’s recent verified organizational change remains Dominique Chokshi’s appointment as Head of Investor Relations. No newly verified leadership developments from the latest processed Labcorp or ARUP items materially changed their management structures.
